skill.displayName: Lingxi-MindVault - Auto Memory Extraction for OpenClaw

llm.summary: The skill's behavior (reading local OpenClaw sessions and pushing their contents to Feishu) matches its description, but there are inconsistencies and risky choices—most notably mismatched metadata (no required envs declared) and a prompt that embeds tokens/IDs and sends full conversation content to an agent—so you should review and limit secrets and scope before installing.

dimensions.detail: The declared purpose (scan OpenClaw sessions → extract → write to Feishu) is consistent with the scripts, but the registry metadata claims no required environment variables or config paths while SKILL.md and the scripts require multiple Feishu credentials and a workspace/.env. That metadata mismatch is misleading and could cause accidental use of example IDs/author IDs.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md + scripts explicitly read full session files under the OpenClaw sessions directory and send extracted content to Feishu. That is consistent with purpose, but the prompt-building step injects L2_APP_TOKEN, L2_TABLE_ID, L3_DOC_ID, L4_DOC_ID and other runtime values directly into the prompt passed to openclaw agent; this unnecessarily exposes credentials/IDs in the agent message and potentially to model logs or other outputs. The scripts also assume the openclaw CLI and agent exist and will be invoked with large prompts containing secrets.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No remote downloads or package installs—this is instruction-only with two bash scripts. That lowers supply-chain risk. However the user must manually copy and run these scripts (crontab), so local execution risk depends on whether you trust the scripts; they do perform json parsing and external tool invocation.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The environment variables the scripts require (FEISHU_USER_OPEN_ID, L2_APP_TOKEN, L2_TABLE_ID, L3_DOC_ID, L4_DOC_ID, optional SESSIONS_DIR/NOTIFY_TARGET) are appropriate for writing to Feishu, but the skill manifest did not declare them. More importantly, the scripts embed these tokens/IDs into the prompt passed to the agent (i.e., copying secrets into a message body), which increases the chance those secrets are exposed to logs, stored prompts, or downstream services. There are no unrelated credentials requested, but the secret-handling approach is risky.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not set always:true, does not modify other skills, and requires manual crontab installation. It creates workspace-local files (.extracted_sessions) and uses /tmp locks; these are expected for its operation and are not excessive by themselves.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill will read your local OpenClaw session files and push extracted content into Feishu. Before installing: (1) don't rely on the registry metadata—SKILL.md requires FEISHU_USER_OPEN_ID, L2_APP_TOKEN, L2_TABLE_ID, L3_DOC_ID, L4_DOC_ID in workspace/.env; (2) avoid using high-privilege or personal tokens—create limited-scope Feishu credentials and test in a disposable account; (3) review and if possible remove the practice of embedding tokens/IDs into the AI prompt (change the agent/tool invocation to read env vars directly) to avoid leaking secrets into prompts or logs; (4) confirm you trust the author and that none of the sessions contain sensitive data you cannot send to Feishu or external models; (5) run the scripts in a sandbox first and verify that openclaw CLI/agent behavior is acceptable and that notifications/writes go only to addresses you control. If you want a safer posture, request the author to (A) update the manifest to declare required env vars, (B) stop interpolating secrets into prompts, and (C) document the minimum token scopes needed.
